LESSON: SIGN READING 13.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Sign Reading 13.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 13.2.1 Fluency, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to sign read at the right speed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 13.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: Interacting with digital technology as the learner uses digital devices to record themselves

as they their sign reading during the readers theatre activity.

● Self-efficacy: as learners improve their speed in Sign Reading.

Values:
Responsibility: as the learner takes up different roles in collaborative activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life-skills: Effective communication as the learner sign reads fluently.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses the reading fluency skills acquired when reading texts in all learning areas

Suggested Learning Resources

Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, Dictionary, Internet, Audio-visual recordings,
